title: Places to See Snow in India: Where and When Snowfall Is Likely

metaDescription: Where to see snow in India: Gulmarg, Sonamarg, Manali and Solang, Kufri and Narkanda, Auli, Tawang and Sela, North Sikkim and Tsomgo, with likely months and caveats.
description: A guide to places to see snow in India and when snow is most likely: Gulmarg, Sonamarg and Pahalgam in Kashmir, Solang, Sissu and the Shimla hills in Himachal, Auli and Chopta in Uttarakhand, Tsomgo, Nathu La and North Sikkim, and Tawang and Sela in Arunachal, plus snow in spring and early summer at high passes, snow activities, and why snowfall is never guaranteed.
dek: Seeing snow is a highlight of many Indian holidays. Here is where it is most likely, in which months, and how to plan around its uncertainty.

hero.alt: Snow-covered slopes and visitors at Gulmarg, Kashmir

intro: Snow in India falls across the Himalaya from roughly December to March, with January and February usually the most reliable months at hill-station heights. Higher places, such as mountain passes and valleys in Sikkim and Arunachal, can hold snow into April and May.
No destination can promise snow on particular dates. The places below are where it is most likely; keep plans flexible and check forecasts and road status close to travel.
quickAnswer: The best places to see snow in India are Gulmarg, Sonamarg and Pahalgam in Kashmir; Solang, Sissu (through the Atal Tunnel), Kufri and Narkanda in Himachal Pradesh; Auli and Chopta in Uttarakhand; Tsomgo Lake, Nathu La and North Sikkim; and Tawang and the Sela Pass in Arunachal Pradesh. Snow is most likely from late December to February; high passes can hold snow into spring. Snowfall is never guaranteed.
takeaways: January and February are usually the most reliable months for snow at hill-station heights.
Gulmarg is the most dependable snow resort, and the centre of skiing.
From Manali, Solang and Sissu (via the Atal Tunnel) are the likeliest spots; Rohtang is closed to tourists in winter.
In spring, snow lingers at high places such as Tsomgo, Zero Point in North Sikkim, Sela and Rohtang when it opens.
Heavy snow closes roads; build in buffer days and check advisories.

items.name: Gulmarg, Sonamarg and Pahalgam
body: Gulmarg is the most reliable snow resort in India, with ski slopes and the gondola; Sonamarg and Pahalgam are snowbound in mid-winter.

items.name: Manali, Solang and Sissu
body: Solang valley is the classic snow spot near Manali; the Atal Tunnel leads to Sissu in Lahaul, snowy in winter. Rohtang Pass is closed to tourists in winter and opens in summer with an online permit.

items.name: Shimla, Kufri and Narkanda
body: Shimla town gets snow in some winters; Kufri and Narkanda, higher up, are more reliable.

items.name: Auli and Chopta
body: Auli's slopes above Joshimath and the winter trail to Tungnath from Chopta; Mussoorie and Dhanaulti see occasional snow.

items.name: Tsomgo, North Sikkim, Tawang and Sela
body: High lakes and passes that often hold snow into spring, reached with permits.

sections.heading: Snow activities
list: Skiing and snowboarding at Gulmarg, Auli, Solang and Narkanda, with registered instructors.
Sledging and snow play at Gulmarg, Solang, Kufri and Patnitop.
Snow treks such as Kedarkantha, Brahmatal and Tungnath-Chandrashila from December to March.
Snowshoe walks and winter photography in Kashmir and Sikkim.

sections.heading: With children, or as a couple
paras: For families, Gulmarg, Solang, Kufri and Patnitop have easy snow play close to roads and facilities; keep outings short and children well layered. Couples often choose Gulmarg, Pahalgam, Auli or Lachung for a quieter snowy stay. Wherever you go, confirm heating, hot water and road access at your stay.

sections.heading: Planning around uncertainty
list: Aim for January and February if snow is the priority.
Choose a higher base (Gulmarg, Narkanda, Auli) over a lower town.
Keep a buffer day in case roads close.
Check forecasts and official road status a few days before, and again on the day.
Have a plan B that is enjoyable without snow.

safety: Snowfall varies from year to year and is never guaranteed; watch forecasts and keep your dates flexible.
Mountain roads close or slow down after heavy rain, snow or landslides; check road and weather updates, and avoid driving after dark.
Permits, e-passes, ropeways and pass openings change; check official portals before you travel.
Heed avalanche advisories and never go off-piste without guides.
Frostbite and hypothermia are real risks; dress in layers and stay dry.
packing: Thermal layers and an insulated jacket

faqs.q: Where can I see snow in India?
faqs.a: Gulmarg, Sonamarg, Solang near Manali, Kufri and Narkanda, Auli, Tsomgo in Sikkim and Tawang are among the likeliest places.

faqs.q: When does it snow in India?
faqs.a: Mostly from late December to February at hill-station heights; higher passes can hold snow into spring.

faqs.q: Is snowfall guaranteed in Gulmarg or Manali?
faqs.a: No; snowfall varies every year, though Gulmarg is the most reliable.

faqs.q: Where can I see snow in summer?
faqs.a: High places such as Rohtang (when open), Zero Point in North Sikkim, Sela Pass and Apharwat above Gulmarg can have snow into May or June.

faqs.q: Which snow destination is best for families?
faqs.a: Gulmarg, Solang, Kufri and Patnitop have easy snow play near roads and facilities.
